practice.development[1]: The mathematics is correct, but the booklet never asks students to classify the arc on which a supplied angle stands as major or minor. Replace this with an adapted Development naming-angle question; recognising these arc terms is not the central target skill.

practice.development[2]: The mathematics is correct, but major/minor classification of the arc intercepted by a supplied angle is not an asked booklet type. Replace this with an adapted Development naming-angle question.

practice.development[4]: The answer is correct, but evaluating competing claims and explaining angle-letter order is not an asked booklet type. Replace this with a direct adapted Development question naming the circumference angle.

practice.development[6]: The chord-naming part is supported by Development 8(a), lines 328–334. The added request to name an already-named minor arc is tautological and is not an asked booklet type; remove that request and its corresponding answer, retaining the supported chord task.

practice.mastery[1]: Parts (a–b) are supported naming tasks. Part (c), explaining why a supplied angle is not subtended by a chord, is not an asked booklet type; remove or replace that part with a supported naming task while retaining the valid parts.

practice.mastery[2]: Parts (a–b) match the booklet's central-angle and paired circumference-angle naming tasks. Part (c) reverses the booklet's given-arc-to-angle task: naming/classifying the intercepted arc from supplied angles is not asked. Remove or replace that part with a supported naming task.

quiz.q6: The answer and distractor explanations are correct, but classifying the intercepted arc as major/minor is not an asked booklet type. Replace q6 with an adapted booklet naming-angle question, retaining its id.
summary: Replaced three Development tasks and quiz q6 with direct booklet-supported angle-naming questions, updating their structure slugs and adding all missing booklet citations. Removed only the unsupported arc request from practice.development[6] and part (c) from practice.mastery[1] and practice.mastery[2], retaining every whole item and preserving all other content.
reviewSummary: All seven requested items have correct answers, consistent diagrams and usable working, and match question types explicitly asked in the supplied booklet. The theory correctly explains subtended angles and standing arcs, and quiz.q6 has exactly one correct option with accurate distractor explanations.
